Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

```bash

```

### install(app, options)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/variables/VueQueryPlugin.md

Installs a QueryClient on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through useQueryClient. Accepts options to provide an existing QueryClient instance or client configuration.

```APIDOC
### Method Signature
```ts
install: (app: any, options?: VueQueryPluginOptions) => void
```

### Description
Installs a `QueryClient` on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through `useQueryClient` — the Vue equivalent of React's `QueryClientProvider`, but wired up as an app-level plugin instead of a wrapping component.

### Parameters
- **app** (`any`) - The Vue application instance.
- **options** (`VueQueryPluginOptions`, default: `{}`) - Optional plugin options including `queryClient` or `queryClientConfig`.

### Returns
- `void`

### Examples
```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const app = createApp(App)
app.use(VueQueryPlugin)
```

Passing a custom `queryClient` instance:
```ts
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })
```

Passing `queryClientConfig`:
```ts
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, {
  queryClientConfig: {
    defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 5 * 1000 } },
  },
})
```
```

### Invalidate queries by key prefix

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/query-invalidation.md

Invalidates matching queries starting with the specified queryKey prefix. In this example, both the base 'todos' and the parameterized 'todos' queries are invalidated.

```ts
import { injectQuery, QueryClient } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'

class QueryInvalidationExample {
  readonly queryClient = inject(QueryClient)

  invalidateQueries() {
    this.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
  }

  // Both queries below will be invalidated
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos', { page: 1 }],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
}
```

--------------------------------

### useQueryClient(id)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue's inject. Must be called inside setup() or another function that supports an injection context.

```APIDOC
## useQueryClient(id)

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Signature
```ts
function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient;
```

### Parameters
- **id** (`string`, optional, default: `''`) - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app.

### Returns
- **QueryClient** - The retrieved `QueryClient` instance.

### Throws
- Throws if called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

--------------------------------

### Basic TanStack Solid Query setup with useQuery and QueryClientProvider

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Wrap the application in a QueryClientProvider and pass a QueryClient instance. Inside components, use useQuery with an accessor function returning query options and handle loading, error, and success states using SolidJS control flow components.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.error}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Fetch data with useQuery in a component

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/vue-query/README.md

Call useQuery in the setup method of a component by passing an object containing queryKey and queryFn.

```tsx
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

export default defineComponent({
  name: 'MyComponent',
  setup() {
    const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

    return {
      query,
    }
  },
})
```

### Install VueQueryPlugin with a custom QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/variables/VueQueryPlugin.md

Pass a custom QueryClient instance to VueQueryPlugin, useful for SSR request isolation or usage outside Vue components.

```ts
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

### Configure TestBed with a fresh QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/testing.md

Sets up TestBed with an isolated QueryClient instance configured with retry disabled for faster test failures. Use provideTanStackQuery or provideQueryClient to provide it in test modules without including withDevtools.

```ts
const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      retry: false, // ✅ faster failure tests
    },
  },
})

TestBed.configureTestingModule({
  providers: [provideTanStackQuery(queryClient)],
})
```

### createQueriesController(host, options, queryClient?)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createQueriesController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to multiple queries. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes current and destroy methods.

```APIDOC
### Signature

```ts
function createQueriesController<TQueryOptions, TCombinedResult>(
  host: ReactiveControllerHost,
  options: Accessor<CreateQueriesControllerOptions<TQueryOptions, TCombinedResult>>,
  queryClient?: QueryClient
): QueriesResultAccessor<TCombinedResult>;
```

### Description
Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to multiple queries. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes `current` and `destroy`. When `options` or `options.queries` is a function, it is re-read during host updates so the query list can follow reactive host state. If `queryClient` is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected `QueryClientProvider`.

### Type Parameters
- **TQueryOptions** (`extends any[]`)
- **TCombinedResult** (`= CreateQueriesResults<TQueryOptions>`)

### Parameters
- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the queries subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateQueriesControllerOptions<TQueryOptions, TCombinedResult>>`) - Queries controller options, or a getter that returns options.
- **queryClient** (`QueryClient`, optional) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns
- **QueriesResultAccessor<TCombinedResult>** - An accessor for the latest query results, or the value returned by `combine`.

### Example

```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createQueriesController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class DashboardView extends LitElement {
  private readonly dashboard = createQueriesController(this, {
    queries: [
      { queryKey: ['stats'], queryFn: fetchStats },
      { queryKey: ['projects'], queryFn: fetchProjects },
    ],
    combine: ([stats, projects]) => ({
      stats: stats.data,
      projects: projects.data ?? [],
      isPending: stats.isPending || projects.isPending,
    }),
  })

  render() {
    const dashboard = this.dashboard()
    return html`<p>Projects: ${dashboard.projects.length}</p>`
  }
}
```
```

### useIsFetching(host, filters, queryClient)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/useIsFetching.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that tracks how many matching queries are currently fetching. When filters is a function, it is re-read during host updates so the count follows reactive host state. If queryClient is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected QueryClientProvider.

```APIDOC
## useIsFetching

### Description
Creates a Lit reactive controller that tracks how many matching queries are currently fetching. When `filters` is a function, it is re-read during host updates so the count can follow reactive host state.

### Syntax
```ts
function useIsFetching(
   host: ReactiveControllerHost,
   filters?: Accessor<QueryFilters<readonly unknown[]>>,
   queryClient?: QueryClient
): IsFetchingAccessor;
```

### Parameters
- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the cache subscription.
- **filters** (`Accessor<QueryFilters<readonly unknown[]>>`, optional) - Query filters, or a getter that returns query filters. Defaults to `{}`.
- **queryClient** (`QueryClient`, optional) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns
- `IsFetchingAccessor` - An accessor for the current number of matching fetching queries.

### Example
```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { useIsFetching } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class TodosStatus extends LitElement {
  private readonly todosFetching = useIsFetching(this, {
    queryKey: ['todos'],
  })

  render() {
    return html`<span>${this.todosFetching()} active todo fetches</span>`
  }
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Create static and reactive Accessor instances

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/type-aliases/Accessor.md

Demonstrates initializing an Accessor with a static array or a reactive zero-argument getter that depends on host state.

```typescript
const staticKey: Accessor<readonly unknown[]> = ['todos']
const reactiveKey: Accessor<readonly unknown[]> = () => ['todos', this.userId]
```

### Define component props in Vue script setup

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reactivity.md

Defines component props using defineProps in Vue script setup syntax with TypeScript.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const props = defineProps<{
  userId: string
}>()
</script>
```

### Install @tanstack/vue-query-devtools with Yarn

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/devtools.md

Installs the dedicated Vue Query devtools package via Yarn. Devtools are automatically excluded in production builds when NODE_ENV is not development.

```bash

```
